outcomes.text: Name objects around them such as trees, water, animals and sky.
Tell the weather outside from the sun, heat or cold, rain, wind and dust.
Show how they feel about their surroundings: cold, hot, fresh or bad air.
Show care for nature by knowing living things feel pain too.
Observe living things and describe what they see to peers.
Name the right clothes for different weather.
Understand how long spells of cold, hot, windy, rainy or dry weather make seasons.
Say how they feel about hot and cold weather and share a favourite weather with a reason.

subtopics.title: Seasons at home and caring for plants (ECE-2)

outcomes.text: Talk with elders at home about seasons and which fruits and vegetables grow in each.
Take part in nature activities like watering plants and caring for living things.
Name common local plants and animals.
Treat animals kindly and gently.
Plant and care for a local plant with adult help.
Share stories about caring for animals.
Identify common local plants and animals.
Explain why different animals and plants are important.
Care for a pet or make a bird feeder with adult supervision.
Take one action to protect the environment after stories about animals' habitats.

topics.title: Human Relation to the Natural Environment

outcomes.text: Observe how people depend on nature for food, air and water.
Share food experiences and likes and dislikes respectfully.
Recognise that everyone has different preferences.
Add a variety of fruits and vegetables to meals.
Sort food into fruits, vegetables and grains.
Appreciate different local and cultural foods.
Respect what others do and eat culturally.
Try new healthy foods and limit unhealthy ones.
Identify the sun, air and water through sensory experiences.
Appreciate nature, for example that the sun helps plants grow.
Act out how pollution can harm animals and people.
Recognise pollution and its sources such as cars and factories.
Identify simple actions that keep land, air and water clean.
Reduce pollution by not littering, saving water and switching off lights.
Join activities like planting, cleaning up and saving water.
Observe that the sun gives heat important for life.
Observe what happens to things like ice when warmed by the sun.
Appreciate the sun as keeping us warm and giving light.
Give animals water on a hot day.
Practise simple safety in extreme weather, and sun safety with a hat.
Show how the sun warms the Earth.
Observe melting when things warm up.
Discuss feelings about pets and harsh weather through stories.
Act out staying safe in bad weather such as storms, rain or smog.

subtopics.title: Fairness and clean air and water (ECE-1)

outcomes.text: Spot fair and unfair situations such as sharing toys.
Recognise that clean air and water are needed for everyone's health.
Practise sharing and taking turns.
Make a handprint poster with small promises like not wasting water.
Notice unfair treatment and suggest ways to make it fair.
Listen to a story about children with and without clean air and water and share ideas to help.
Say how they feel when something is unfair.
Take turns at classroom cleaning tasks.
Draw a poster on why a clean environment matters to all living things.

units.title: Domain C: Sustainable Living and Stewardship

topics.title: Engagement with nature, sustainable lifestyle & waste management

outcomes.text: Understand why keeping spaces clean matters.
Identify ways to protect natural resources: food, air and water.
Sort clean and dirty objects in a game.
Join a clean-up walk and talk about why it matters.
Do small sustainable acts such as switching off lights or reusing paper.
Name simple sustainable actions through stories and discussion.
Make crafts from recycled materials.
Draw or craft ways to care for the environment, such as recycling.
Tell stories about helping keep the house clean.
Put trash in the correct bins.

topics.title: Renewable energy use, responsible consumption and conservation

outcomes.text: Understand that fast-moving things like wind, water and sun have energy people can use.
Tell needs from wants.
Remind others to switch off lights.
Say how they feel about wasted food, toys or clothes.
Save water with adult help.
Show patience when sharing resources.
Identify ways electricity is generated, such as wind, water, waves and sunlight.
Tell basic needs from wants in energy use with real examples.
Value resources, for example by not wasting food and giving away spare clothes and toys.
Know that switching off fans, lights and TV saves electricity.
Prefer sharing items such as toys and storybooks over solo use.
